q: A particle has velocity v = t² − 4t + 3 m/s. What is its speed at t = 2 s?
x: v(2) = 4 − 8 + 3 = −1 m/s, so it is moving backwards with speed |−1| = 1 m/s. Speed is the size of the velocity and is never negative.

q: A particle has velocity v = 2t + 3 m/s. How far does it travel during the third second, from t = 2 s to t = 3 s?
x: v > 0 throughout, so distance = ∫₂³ (2t + 3) dt = [t² + 3t]₂³ = 18 − 10 = 8 m. 18 m is the distance in the first three seconds and 9 is v(3).

q: A particle has displacement s = 6t² − t³ metres for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4 s. What is its greatest velocity in this interval?
x: v = 12t − 3t² and a = 12 − 6t = 0 at t = 2, where v = 24 − 12 = 12 m/s; this is a maximum since a changes from positive to negative. 32 m is the greatest displacement, at t = 4.

q: A particle starts from rest with acceleration a = 6 − 2t m/s². At what time does it next come to rest?
x: v = 6t − t² (v = 0 at t = 0), so v = t(6 − t) is zero again at t = 6 s. At t = 3 s the acceleration is zero and the speed is greatest.

q: A particle has displacement s = 5 sin 2t. How is its acceleration a related to s?
x: v = 10 cos 2t and a = −20 sin 2t = −4(5 sin 2t) = −4s. Forgetting to square the factor 2 gives −2s.

q: Particles P and Q leave the origin together at t = 0 along the same line. P has velocity 2t m/s and Q a constant velocity 4 m/s. How far from the origin are they when they next meet?
x: P's displacement is t² and Q's is 4t. They meet when t² = 4t, i.e. t = 4 s, at 16 m. At t = 2 s their velocities are equal, but P is at 4 m and Q at 8 m.

q: A particle has velocity v = 1/(t + 1) m/s. What is its displacement from t = 0 to t = e − 1 seconds?
x: s = ∫₀^(e − 1) dt/(t + 1) = [ln(t + 1)] from 0 to e − 1 = ln e − ln 1 = 1 m. 1/e is the velocity at t = e − 1, not the displacement.

q: A particle starts from rest at the origin with acceleration a = 6t − 6 m/s². At what time does it return to the origin?
x: v = 3t² − 6t and s = t³ − 3t² = t²(t − 3), so s = 0 again at t = 3 s. At t = 2 s it is only momentarily at rest, farthest from the origin (s = −4 m).
